ghCliConsent.title: Read your repositories?
ghCliConsent.body: OpenShip can list your GitHub repositories using the gh CLI you're already logged into.
ghCliConsent.bodyWithLogin: OpenShip can list your GitHub repositories using the gh CLI you're logged into as @{login}.
ghCliConsent.pointNoCloud: Nothing is sent to the cloud — the list never leaves this machine.
ghCliConsent.pointDesktopOnly: Runs only in the desktop app, using your local gh auth.
ghCliConsent.pointReadOnly: Read-only: it lists repos so you can pick one to deploy.

page.title: New Project
page.subtitle: Deploy an app or import your own project.

terminal.title: Connect GitHub
terminal.afterLogin: After logging in, click "Check Connection" to continue.

deviceFlow.title: Sign in to GitHub
deviceFlow.goToSuffix: Enter this code on GitHub to finish signing in.

default.title: Connect GitHub to deploy
default.descSelfHosted: Pick how Openship reaches your repositories.
default.descSaas: Link your GitHub account to browse repos and deploy on every push.
default.cloudAppDesc: Managed GitHub App — deploy to remote servers with short-lived tokens.
default.manualDesc: Set up in Settings — your own GitHub App/OAuth, or this instance's gh CLI. No Openship account.
default.ghCliDesc: Browser sign-in with a device code. No app setup, no SSH, no Openship account.
default.byocDesc: Bring your own credential — a deploy key per server, or a token. No sign-in.

installationPicker.title: Choose GitHub access
installationPicker.description: Select an existing App installation for this workspace.
installationPicker.sharedHint: Using it here keeps your other Openship connections intact.
installationPicker.successDescription: Repository access is ready. You can return to Openship.

folderUpload.emptyFolder: That folder looks empty (or everything was ignored). Pick a project folder.
folderUpload.stackDesc: Pick the stack for your folder — this sets the build environment. You'll upload it next.
folderUpload.uploadSubtitle: Packed in your browser — node_modules, .git and build output are skipped
folderUpload.dropTitle: Drop your project folder or click to browse
folderUpload.dropSubtitle: The whole folder is uploaded and built as a {stack} app

empty.title: No local projects yet
empty.description: Import a project folder from your machine to scan, build, and deploy it locally

form.title: Import from folder
form.dropTitle: Drop a folder here or click to browse
form.dropSubtitle: Select your project folder to auto-detect the framework
form.folderViaBrowser: Folder selected via browser - please enter the full absolute path and press Scan
form.folderDropped: Folder dropped - please enter the full absolute path and press Scan

repositoryList.installDesc: Install the GitHub App on your account or organization to grant access to your repositories.
repositoryList.noMatchingDesc: Try a different search term or adjust your filters
repositoryList.noReposDesc: This account doesn’t have any repositories yet

sidebar.quickTipDesc: Select any repository to deploy it instantly. Configure automatic deployments on every push.
sidebar.footnote: Manage the GitHub connections used to browse and deploy repositories.

urlImport.invalidUrl: Enter a valid GitHub repository URL
urlImport.title: Import from Git URL
urlImport.description: Paste a public repository URL to import. No GitHub connection required.

customAppModal.title: Add a custom app
customAppModal.description: Upload an app definition (JSON). It's added to your catalog and marked unverified.
customAppModal.unverifiedBody: This deploys images you provided — not an official, reviewed app. Review the definition and only add apps you trust.
customAppModal.invalidDefinition: This isn't a valid app definition — check the required fields and references.
customAppModal.onlyTemplateSupported: Only template apps can be added (flow apps aren't supported).

apps.mail: Your own mail on your own domain — SMTP/IMAP, mailboxes and webmail on one server. Or keep the mailboxes you already have and just run the webmail.
apps.supabase: Full self-hosted Supabase — Postgres, Auth, REST, Realtime, Storage, and Studio behind one API gateway.
apps.mongodb: MongoDB document database with the Mongo Express web admin UI.
apps.convex: Self-hosted Convex reactive backend + dashboard, with a persistent data volume.
apps.n8n: Workflow automation — connect apps and APIs with a visual editor.
apps.ghost: Publishing for blogs, newsletters, and membership sites, with a focused editor and your own database.
apps.directus: A headless CMS with REST and GraphQL APIs over your data and a browser-based admin studio.
apps.nocodb: An Airtable-style spreadsheet interface for working with SQL-backed data.
apps.metabase: Business intelligence, questions, and dashboards over your existing data.
apps.grafana: Dashboards and visualization for your metrics and logs, on your own infrastructure.
apps.gitea: Lightweight Git hosting with repositories, issues, and pull requests.
apps.code-server: VS Code in your browser, running against a workspace on your own server.
apps.uptime-kuma: Uptime monitoring with status pages and alerts for your services.
apps.vaultwarden: A lightweight, self-hosted password manager compatible with Bitwarden clients.
apps.freshrss: Your own RSS and Atom feed reader, with a browser interface for organizing feeds.
apps.stirling-pdf: Split, merge, convert, OCR, and edit PDFs on infrastructure you control.
apps.it-tools: A browser-based collection of developer and sysadmin utilities, with no account setup.
apps.excalidraw: Virtual whiteboard for sketches and diagrams. Stateless — drawings save in your browser.
apps.buzz: Self-hostable workspace where humans and AI agents collaborate — chat, code, reviews, and workflows in one audit log.
apps.minio: S3-compatible object storage with a web console — point any S3 client (aws-cli, SDKs) at it, or bind a bucket straight into another project's uploads.
apps.kafka: Apache Kafka event-streaming broker (KRaft mode — no ZooKeeper) with the Kafbat Kafka UI web console for topics, messages, and consumer groups.
apps.qdrant: High-performance vector database for AI search, RAG, and embeddings — with the built-in Qdrant Web UI for browsing collections and running queries.
apps.meilisearch: Lightning-fast, typo-tolerant search engine. Point any Meilisearch client at the URL below with the master key — index your documents and search in milliseconds.
apps.neon: Community-powered self-hosted Neon with Postgres branching, a console, and per-branch connection strings.
apps.posthog: Product analytics, session replay, and feature flags in a self-hosted hobby stack.
apps.redis: In-memory data store for caching, sessions, rate limits, and queues — Valkey, the open-source Redis fork. Drop-in Redis-compatible: point any redis client at it. Ships with RedisInsight, a browser UI that arrives already connected to this instance.
apps.umami: Privacy-friendly, cookie-free web analytics — a self-hosted alternative to Google Analytics. Add one script tag to your site and see traffic in a clean dashboard you own.
apps.webmail: A fast, self-hosted webmail client. Point it at any IMAP/SMTP mailbox — an Openship Mail server, Gmail, Fastmail, or your company's — and read, search and send from a clean UI on your own domain. Nothing is stored outside your server.
apps.clickhouse: Columnar SQL for analytical data, with the CH-UI console for queries and schema browsing.
apps.mindwire: Run coding-agent runtimes behind a self-hosted control plane. MindWire keeps the runtime private and gives you one console to manage agents, credentials, and sessions.
apps.pocketbase: Self-hosted PocketBase with auth, a realtime SQLite database, file storage, and an admin dashboard in one small service.
apps.authentik: An identity provider for SSO, OAuth2, OpenID Connect, and SAML, with its server, worker, and PostgreSQL database.
apps.mariadb: A MySQL-compatible database with a lightweight Adminer control panel for queries, tables, and exports.
apps.nextcloud: Private file sync and sharing with Nextcloud Admin, MariaDB, Redis file locking, and scheduled background jobs.
apps.odoo: Run CRM, sales, inventory, and other Community business apps with PostgreSQL and a ready-to-use administrator account.
apps.postgresql: A persistent PostgreSQL database with pgAdmin for browser-based administration and SQL queries.
apps.rabbitmq: A persistent message broker with the official management dashboard for queues, exchanges, and connections.
apps.wordpress: Publish websites, blogs, and stores with WordPress Admin, a private MariaDB database, and persistent uploads.
